state.case_summary:
A 48-year-old woman with a 7-year history of a submucosal tumour below the esophagogastric junction, monitored periodically since 2004, presented in November 2011 with melena and progressive anemia; her hemoglobin level was 7.5 g/dL. Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen revealed a 70 × 50 × 55 mm hypoechogenic, subcardial mass on the posterior gastric wall. In December 2011, the lesion was resected endoscopically by a piecemeal technique under general anesthesia, and histopathology reportedly confirmed a lipoma. Six weeks later, endoscopic evaluation demonstrated a recurrent bleeding tumour at the same site.
